request.recipient: Intersect Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v for administration on behalf of TxPipe/vendor
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Tx3 by TxPipe as an open API layer for Cardano dApp protocols, including protocol onboarding, developer and agent-facing infrastructure, MCP server, skills framework, documentation, SDKs, and JSON-RPC endpoints.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,308,000 ADA plus a 327,000 ADA contingency reserve over 12 months, with a total withdrawal of 1,684,050 ADA including a 49,050 ADA Intersect administration fee.
Tx3 is presented as a framework where each protocol is described once with a verified interface definition that generates documentation, multi-language SDKs, and live JSON-RPC endpoints.
The proposal states that Catalyst Fund 14 already put the Tx3 developer layer into production with 5 protocols live on the Tx3 Protocol Registry.
The proposal funds 12 additional protocol onboardings, at 3 per quarter, with full developer and agent coverage.
The proposer claims Cardano currently lacks a common interface mechanism across the ecosystem, forcing integrators to relearn each protocol and increasing integration cost.
The proposal claims AI agents will become a major source of on-chain activity and require shared, deterministic, auditable interface layers to reduce risks from hallucinated transactions.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The proposal states the requested withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the moment of submission.
The proposal says independent oversight will be provided by Intersect and technically capable third parties with reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.

The proposal states TxPipe has received funding through 30 Catalyst proposals from Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule, plus Intersect 2025 maintenance funding delivered on schedule.

summary: The document describes a 1,684,050 ADA treasury withdrawal administered by Intersect for TxPipe's Tx3 project, focused on standardized protocol interfaces, additional protocol onboarding, and AI-agent-facing infrastructure, with governance-process references and smart-contract administration details but limited embedded feasibility, risk, alternatives, and budget breakdown detail.
